verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — NVDA Recovers Above Stop; Brent Retreats Below $97; 30Y Day-2 + NFP Pending
verdict.rationale_short: The June 3 night brief's bear scenario did not materialize: NVDA recovered to $227.36 (+4.9% from yesterday's close), confirming AVGO's AI guidance disappointment was company-specific rather than a systemic AI demand signal. Brent retreated to $96.97 — below the $97 mandatory escalation trigger for the first time since the cross — and the 10Y eased to 4.49%, supporting 30Y Day-2 sub-5.0% confirmation. STEP ASIDE maintained at medium conviction: the framework cannot upgrade to HOLD until the 30Y confirms Day-2 sub-5.0% at today's close. Friday's May NFP remains the decisive binary for any directional upgrade.

bear_case: The constructive morning signals — NVDA recovery, Brent retreat, 10Y easing — rest on a fragile premise: that AVGO's FY2027 AI revenue guidance plateau is company-specific and not a leading indicator of hyperscaler capex deceleration. If AVGO's unchanged FY2027 target proves to be the first data point in a series where AI infrastructure demand growth decelerates at the rate-of-change level (even if absolute revenues remain high), then NVDA's next print faces the same whisper-number dynamic at a 38x forward P/E. The House war powers resolution is not a ceasefire — the 2026 Iran war continues into its fourth month, and any resumed escalation re-crosses Brent above $97, potentially toward $100, within hours of a single Gulf attack headline. The S&P 500 at 7,553 on a 22.66x forward P/E is not priced for a scenario where AI capex growth rate plateaus, oil re-escalates, and May NFP prints hot tomorrow. Invalidation: if Brent closes above $100 AND the 30Y closes above 5.05% on the same session, exit all longs — the STEP ASIDE framework cannot hold that combination.
